title: Monotonic Distributed Range Keys (Hotspotting Smell)
damaged_code:
```sql
CREATE TABLE device_metrics (
    timestamp TIMESTAMP, -- Monotonically increasing key
    device_id VARCHAR,
    PRIMARY KEY (timestamp)
);
```
pattern: Using monotonically increasing values (e.g., auto-increment sequences, serials, or timestamps) as the primary/range key in a partitioned distributed database.
why_bad: Forces all concurrent write requests to land on a single partition block (the current end of the range), completely defeating horizontal write scaling and creating severe node bottlenecks.
detection: Distributed schemas where partition keys are derived from sequential sequence generators or system time.
counterexample: Databases running purely on single-node instances without horizontal partitioning. `Contextual`.
fix: Prepend a hash prefix or use hashed UUIDs as keys to evenly distribute write operations across partitions.
